paragraphs: Here's the big idea, friend: what God says, God does. Balak had a king's budget, a king's mountain views and a king's patience, and none of it moved God an inch. Balaam says it plainly: "God is not a man, that He should lie, or a son of man, that He should change His mind." (Numbers 23:19)

Think about how many promises you've heard that fell apart by Tuesday. Balak kept moving Balaam to new spots like a new view was going to change the answer, and I get it, I've moved a cookie tray to a different rack hoping for a miracle. But the blessing didn't depend on the spot. Balaam says, "I have indeed received a command to bless; He has blessed, and I cannot change it." (Numbers 23:20)

So what does that mean for you? The God who brought Israel out of Egypt (Numbers 23:22) is the same God whose word stands, and you can lean your whole weight on it. No spell, no scheme and no amount of silver can undo what He has spoken. That's why my ovens stay ready, friend, because He keeps His word. And this story isn't over, because that third mountain is still waiting.
